en.name: Crème fraîche
en.summary: Crème fraîche is pasteurised cream soured with a mesophilic lactic culture — the same technology as sour cream, at a higher fat content and a gentler acidity. Refrigerated it runs about 2 weeks from purchase, and roughly 7–10 days once the pot is open. Freezing splits it.
en.pantry: There is no counter life for crème fraîche. It is a fresh cultured cream and belongs in the fridge at all times; the culture that makes it tangy does not preserve it. At the table, follow the 2-hour rule, or 1 hour if the room is above 32 °C (90 °F), and spoon out what you need rather than leaving the pot beside a hot dish where it warms and thins.
en.fridge: Keep it at 0–5 °C. Treat about 2 weeks from purchase as the working limit: that is the published figure for commercial sour cream, applied here because the two products are made the same way and crème fraîche's higher fat, if anything, helps. Once the pot is open, our own conservative reading is roughly 7–10 days — not a published number, so err short rather than long. Always use a clean spoon: crème fraîche is much less acidic than yoghurt, and a mould spore or a buttery knife will start a colony. Pink, grey or fuzzy growth means the whole pot goes; mould hyphae run deeper than the visible patch and you cannot scoop the problem out. A little clear whey on top is normal and stirs back in.
en.freezer: Freezing splits crème fraîche, so no timeline is given. The high fat means it survives better than sour cream and can be whisked back together for a sauce, but it will never be a spoonable garnish again — it thaws grainy and weeping. The better answer is to buy small pots. If you already have a tub you cannot finish, cook it out: crème fraîche is stable in a hot pan in a way that sour cream is not, so stir it into a sauce and use that.
spoilage: Any mould — pink, grey, green or fuzzy white — on the surface or the lid.
A yeasty, fizzy or bitter taste beyond the usual clean tang.
A bulging lid or bubbles rising through the pot.
A ropy, stringy texture, or a strong cheesy smell.
tips: Buy the small pot; it does not keep long once opened.
Write the opening date on the lid.
Use the last of a pot in a pan sauce rather than letting it sit.

faq.q: How long does crème fraîche last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 2 weeks from purchase at 0–5 °C, and roughly 7–10 days once opened. The opened figure is our own conservative reading rather than a published one.
It splits, so there is no timeline for it. Thawed, it can be whisked into a sauce but never spooned onto a dish again.

faq.q: Is the watery layer on top a problem?
faq.a: No, that is whey and it stirs back in. Mould, fizz or bitterness is a problem, and means the whole pot goes.

faq.q: Is crème fraîche the same as sour cream?
faq.a: Nearly. Same method, but crème fraîche has more fat and a milder acidity, which is why it can be boiled in a sauce without curdling.

zh.name: 法式酸奶油
zh.summary: 法式酸奶油是用中溫乳酸菌把巴氏殺菌鮮奶油發酵而成，和酸奶油是同一套技術，只是脂肪更高、酸味更柔和。冷藏從購買日起約 2 週，開封後大約 7～10 天。冷凍會讓它分離。
zh.pantry: 法式酸奶油沒有室溫保存這回事。它是生鮮發酵鮮奶油，必須全程冷藏；讓它帶酸的那些菌並不會保存它。上桌時請守 2 小時原則（室溫超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時），要用多少先舀出來，不要把整罐放在熱菜旁邊回溫變稀。
zh.fridge: 放在 0～5 °C。把從購買日起約 2 週當成工作上限：這是市售酸奶油的公告值，套用在這裡是因為兩者製法相同，而法式酸奶油的高脂肪只會更有利。罐子開封後，我們保守的判讀是大約 7～10 天——這不是公告數字，所以寧可抓短不抓長。每次都要用乾淨的湯匙：它的酸度比優格低很多，一顆霉孢子或一把沾了奶油的刀就足以長成一整片。出現粉紅、灰色或絨毛狀的霉，整罐丟掉；霉的菌絲會比看得見的斑塊更深入，不是挖掉就沒事。表面有一點透明乳清是正常的，攪回去即可。
zh.freezer: 冷凍會讓法式酸奶油分離，所以這裡不給期限。它脂肪高，表現比酸奶油好一些，解凍後可以打散拌進醬汁，但再也回不去可以舀在菜上的狀態——解凍後又粗又出水。比較好的做法是買小罐。如果已經有一罐用不完，就加熱用掉：法式酸奶油下熱鍋不像酸奶油那樣容易油水分離，拌成醬汁最省。
spoilage: 表面或蓋子上出現任何霉——粉紅、灰、綠或白色絨毛。
吃起來有酵母味、氣泡感或苦味，超出原本乾淨的酸度。
質地牽絲，或散發強烈的起司臭味。
tips: 每一次都用乾淨的湯匙，沒有例外。
最後剩下的一點就拿去做鍋底醬汁，不要放著。

faq.q: 法式酸奶油放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 0～5 °C 下，從購買日起約 2 週；開封後大約 7～10 天。開封後的數字是我們保守的判讀，不是公告值。

faq.q: 法式酸奶油可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 會分離，所以沒有給期限。解凍後可以打進醬汁，但無法再當作舀在菜上的佐醬。
沒有，那是乳清，攪回去就好。長霉、冒泡或發苦才是問題，整罐都要丟。

faq.q: 法式酸奶油和一般酸奶油一樣嗎？
faq.a: 幾乎一樣。做法相同，但法式酸奶油脂肪更高、酸度更柔，所以煮進醬汁裡不會油水分離。
